message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"5.2","text":"“Yesterday, when I left this place, friends, I admit that I could not get to sleep, because I was deeply preoccupied with the discussion that was going to take place with Appion. As I lay awake, the stratagems I had devised against him in Rome rushed into my mind. They were as follows. From childhood I, Clement, had loved truth, had sought the things that matter to the soul, and had spent my time on refutations and demonstrations; but because I could find nothing definitive, under the strain of my thoughts I ran aground in illness. And indeed, while I lay ill, Appion arrived in Rome. He was a friend of my father and stayed as my guest. When he learned that I was bedridden, he came in to see me, since he was not unversed in medicine, and asked why I had taken to bed. I was well aware that the man held Jews in deep hatred—so much so that he had written many books against them—and that he had now taken Simon himself as a friend, not out of a love of learning, but because he knew him to be a Samaritan, a Jew-hater, and someone who had come forward against the Jews. For that reason he had drawn him close, so that he could learn from him something to use against the Jews—","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς πρὸς Ἀππίωνα μελλούσης ἔσεσθαι ζητήσεως","chosen":"the discussion that was going to take place with Appion","rationale":"ζήτησις can denote an inquiry, dispute, or debate. “Discussion” leaves its precise character open while the wider narrative supplies its adversarial aspect."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ἐν Ῥώμῃ πρὸς αὐτόν μοι μεμηχανημένα","chosen":"the stratagems I had devised against him in Rome","rationale":"μηχανάομαι denotes contriving or devising, while πρὸς αὐτόν is contextually adversarial rather than merely relational."},{"source_quote":"εἰς ἀνασκευὰς καὶ κατασκευὰς","chosen":"on refutations and demonstrations","rationale":"The paired terms denote arguments that respectively dismantle and establish a position; alternatives include “disproofs and proofs” or “negative and positive arguments.”"},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τῆς συνοίας ἐξώκειλα εἰς νόσον","chosen":"under the strain of my thoughts I ran aground in illness","rationale":"σύνοια can denote intense thought, anxiety, or distress arising from reflection. The rendering “strain of my thoughts” preserves that range, while “ran aground” retains the nautical image in ἐξώκειλα rather than reducing it to a generic transition into illness."},{"source_quote":"πατρικὸς ὢν μοι φίλος","chosen":"He was a friend of my father","rationale":"πατρικὸς φίλος can mean a paternal or inherited family friend. The immediate first-person construction most naturally indicates a friend connected with Clement’s father."},{"source_quote":"σαμαρέα αὐτὸν οἶδεν μισοϊουδαῖόν τε ὄντα","chosen":"he knew him to be a Samaritan, a Jew-hater","rationale":"The ethnic designation and the compound μισοϊουδαῖος are retained distinctly rather than treating Samaritan identity itself as equivalent to hatred of Jews."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἵνα δύνατο κατὰ Ἰουδαίων τι παρ’ αὐτοῦ μανθάνειν","issue":"The form δύνατο after ἵνα is morphosyntactically unusual by classical standards but can be understood as late or nonclassical use of a past indicative in a purpose clause. The proposed optative is only a possible normalization, not the supplied reading.","proposed_reading":"ἵνα δύναιτο κατὰ Ἰουδαίων τι παρ’ αὐτοῦ μανθάνειν","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
